title: Tenant warmup suppression from allocator lease-stamp skew causing SLA breaches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated tenants experienced elevated 95th/99th latency and prolonged cold-starts during multi-region failover windows. Investigation indicates an allocator 'lease-stamp skew' bug that caused the warmup coordinator to treat recently-warmed slots as stale, evicting them or suppressing warmup signals. The immediate effect: reserved pools reported available headroom, but tenant warmup progression stalled, leading to burst limit exhaustion and customer SLA breaches for burst-heavy workloads.

Root cause hypothesis: The allocator writes a per-slot lease stamp after warmup completes. During failover/reconciliation, a race between the lease propagator and the warmup tracker could leave the tracker with an older lease view. The warmup tracker then misclassifies slots as warmup-ineligible and either evicts them prematurely or disables incremental warmup credits. This manifests as sudden suppression of warmup traffic even though pool-level metrics show capacity, so fallback routing and burst-safety mechanisms do not trigger fast enough.

Impact: Affected customers saw sustained 10-30s increased tail latency and request throttling during short surge windows; some experienced failed requests when burst budgets were drained. Incidents were observed across two customers with high small-tenant concurrency and one internal Canary.

Reproduction steps: 1) Deploy allocator + lease-propagator with synthetic network delay between regions. 2) Simulate tenant warmup completion while triggering a replicaset rotation. 3) Observe warmup tracker telemetry and slot-state transitions in Grafana panel 'allocator.slot_state'.

Immediate mitigations completed: - Short-term patch to the warmup tracker to tolerate lease timestamp gaps (<15s) and avoid evicting in-flight warm slots (hotfix deployed 2025-11-03). - Temporarily widened burst-safety fallback to consider pool-level KV cache occupancy (deployed 2025-11-04) to accelerate fallback routing for affected tenants. - Customer comms: proactive notices and manual capacity top-ups for two impacted customers; compensatory credits issued.

Long-term plan: 1) Implement atomic lease-stamp reconciliation in allocator (PR linked below) so warmup and lease propagation converge deterministically. 2) Add conservative read-after-write barrier in the warmup path to ensure local view correctness during replicaset transitions. 3) Extend the autoscaler policy to detect warmup-suppression signals (slot churn with stable headroom) and automatically trigger graceful fallback routing. 4) Add unit+integration tests that inject lease-propagation delays. 5) Run a canary rollout with synthetic surge workload before full production rollout.

Acceptance criteria: - No warmup suppression observed under injected lease-propagation delays in integration tests. - Warmup completion latency SLO improved by 50% in canary region under the failure scenario. - Post-fix incident recurrence rate = 0 for 30 days in production.

Notes and trade-offs: The read-after-write barrier adds an extra confirmation round to warmup completion which may add ~50-100ms to the tail of warmup completion signals; we consider this acceptable given the reduction in large-scale SLA impacts. The alternative (more invasive allocator redesign) was deprioritized to deliver a lower-risk, faster fix before the holiday traffic window.
comments: 2025-11-02 — SRE (Jon Kim): Alerting detected spike in 99th latency for tenant-acme-co during region failover. Escalated to on-call infra. Noted odd slot churn on allocator-3 in us-west-2.

2025-11-03 — Investigation (Aisha Patel): Correlated allocator slot_state with warmup-tracker logs. Observed lease_stamp regression in 3/4 cases; created this ticket and pushed emergency guard patch to avoid evictions (hotfix: GH#rwd/infra/PR-8421).

2025-11-03 — Hotfix (Marco Ruiz): Deployed warmup-tolerance patch to prod (runbook step executed: avoid-evict-hot-slots). Monitored Grafana panels (allocator.slot_state, warmup.progress). Immediate reduction in eviction events but tail latency still elevated for bursts.

2025-11-04 — SRE (Priya Desai): Enabled temporary fallback heuristic to consider KV cache occupancy for expedited fallback routing. This reduced throttling events for affected tenants. Logged rollback plan in runbook.
2025-11-05 — PM (Evan Liu): Customer updates sent to two affected accounts with summary and compensatory credits. Customers accepted the mitigation plan and requested postmortem.

2025-11-06 — Eng (Marco Ruiz): Drafted allocator reconciliation design doc on Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CAP/Lease+Stamp+Reconciliation. Design reviewed by infra and runtime teams; feedback to add integration test harness.
2025-11-10 — QA (Diane Cheng): Integration tests for injected lease-propagation delays added to CI; initial test run failed (race not fully covered). Working with Marco to extend harness.
2025-11-12 — Eng Lead (Olga Ivanova): Approved hotfix branch for canary rollout. Plan: canary in us-west-2 for 24h with synthetic burst workload, then 3-region staggered rollout if metrics stable.
Next steps: finish tests, merge PR, schedule canary, update runbook and alerts to detect warmup-suppression signature.
